Subject: Nebula-3B showing rising 5xx/timeouts (prod)

Hi Diego —

We're seeing a sharp uptick in 5xx errors and request timeouts from calls routed to nebula-3b over the last ~30 minutes. Error rate climbed from ~0.5% to ~7% and a number of sessions are timing out. This started around 07:35 PST. Impact: several BrightLeaf user-facing features that rely on generation are returning errors; our feature flagging shows a 15% drop in successful completions.

Attached is a short sample from our side (nebula3b-error-sample.log). Key details: requests with >1k token contexts seem overrepresented but we also see shorter requests failing intermittently.

Can you confirm if this is a known issue and share any immediate mitigation steps? We're ready to route traffic if you recommend a fallback.

Thanks — appreciate the quick help.

Camille Roy

Thanks Camille — we're on it.

Internal triage notes (initial):
- Confirmed spike in 5xx and timeouts for model id nebula-3b in us-west-2 between 07:30-08:00 PST.
- Error surface: mix of 5xx (502/503) and backend timeouts; correlation with requests that hit the KV cache eviction path and long KV lifetimes.
- Current impact estimate: ~6.8% error rate for BrightLeaf traffic, ~2% for other customers in same pool.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:00):
1) Shifted BrightLeaf traffic to model nebula-3b-v2 (a patched variant with kernel rollback) for 40% of requests to reduce error exposure.
2) Enabled a conservative per-customer rate limit and short-circuit fallback to nebula-2b-quant for requests that exceed latency threshold (configured at 3s).
3) Increased KV cache TTLs temporarily to prevent frequent eviction storms while we investigate.

Next steps for engineering:
- Rishi: collect kernel telemetry and stack traces for failed requests; grab GC/memory histograms from affected hosts.
- Soojin: prepare an ops runbook for manual traffic split and coordinate with infra to isolate problematic nodes.
- Diego: communicate immediate mitigation plan to BrightLeaf and monitor for improvement.

I'll update Camille in ~2 hours or sooner if we see regression.

Diego Fernandez
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Nebula-3B incident: interim postmortem and next steps

Camille / BrightLeaf team —

Thank you for your patience while our engineers completed the initial investigation. Below is a short interim postmortem and recovery summary. We'll follow up with a full postmortem doc in the next 72 hours.

Summary of impact:
- Window: 2027-01-18 07:30 PST -> 2027-01-18 11:40 PST (primary spike), with intermittent blips through 2027-01-19 as mitigations rolled out.
- Affected model: nebula-3b (inference kernel change), BrightLeaf traffic saw a peak error rate of ~7.1% and ~12% of user sessions experienced at least one generation failure.
- No data leakage or security impact observed.

Root cause (interim):
- A recent optimization to the attention kernel (deployed 2027-01-17) introduced a memory fragmentation pattern that interacted poorly with long-lived KV cache entries and resulted in periodic OOM-related 5xxs under certain request shapes.

What we did:
1) Rolled back the experimental kernel on affected hosts (completed 09:00 PST 2027-01-18).
2) Deployed nebula-3b-v2 (patched binary with kernel rollback) and progressively shifted customer traffic.
3) Added conservative latency-based fallbacks to nebula-2b-quant for high-risk requests.
4) Tuned KV cache eviction heuristics to avoid eviction storms.

Resolution status:
- Immediate stability restored for BrightLeaf by the progressive traffic split and kernel rollback.
- A permanent fix (kernel patch with additional memory-safety checks) is scheduled and will be deployed after internal validation. Estimated ETA for targeted permanent rollback+patch: 2027-01-26.

Follow-ups and action items:
- Infra/Runtime: full heap/fragmentation telemetry dashboard (owner: Rishi) — due 2027-01-24.
- Runtime: automated canary for kernel changes that simulates long-KV lifetimes (owner: Soojin) — due 2027-02-04.
- Customer success: offer a post-incident credits discussion if BrightLeaf requests (owner: Marissa) — due 2027-01-25.

We apologize for the disruption. The team recognizes the operational impact this had on your product and we're treating this with high priority. If you saw any residual issues after 21 Jan 15:00 PST, please let me know and we'll pull logs immediately.

Attached: nebula3b-postmortem-draft.docx (interim notes).
